channel.title: Kubai Kevin
channel.description: Practical backend engineering, AI tooling, and developer career advice by Kubai Kevin — a software developer with 10+ years building production systems in fintech and AI.

item.title: Debugging techniques that outlast any framework
item.description: Framework-agnostic debugging methods: narrow hypotheses about state, time, concurrency, boundaries and data shape, with a worked race-condition example.

item.title: SLOs for agentic features: beyond latency
item.description: Define agent SLOs on task success, tool-call validity and clean termination, instrument them with OpenTelemetry, and alert on error-budget burn.

item.title: Cross-border fintech: why your KYC fails in Dakar
item.description: Why KYC validation breaks across borders, and how to replace per-country code forks with a policy layer, reachability checks, and locale-safe schemas.

item.title: Fraud detection: rules vs scoring, where they meet
item.description: How to split fraud decisions between a deterministic rules gate and a calibrated scoring model, with a worked three-layer architecture and audit trail.

item.title: AI best practices fail on slow networks
item.description: Why LLM best practices break on high-latency, metered mobile links, and how to design around a request budget of round trips and bytes instead.

item.title: SBOM + attestation that gets used
item.description: How to generate, sign, attach and enforce SBOMs and build attestations so admission control and CI gates reject unverified artifacts.

item.title: LLM evals: LangSmith vs Promptfoo in prod
item.description: How to choose between hosted trace-based eval platforms and local CLI eval runners, with latency, cost, CI and data-residency tradeoffs.

item.title: Webhook delivery that survives outages
item.description: How to build durable webhook delivery with a transactional outbox, at-least-once queues, idempotency keys, and a retry schedule that outlasts outages.

item.title: Who signs off on AI code?
item.description: AI coding assistants produce diffs fast, but accountability still needs a named human. Here is a review workflow with hooks, policy checks, and failure modes.

item.title: Double-entry ledger: concurrent write errors
item.description: Why concurrent writes corrupt double-entry ledgers, and how to enforce the debit-equals-credit invariant with isolation, locks, and triggers.

item.title: Agentic workflows: surviving network partitions
item.description: How to keep agentic workflows correct when networks drop: idempotency keys, an outbox with stable action IDs, and reconciliation on reconnect.

item.title: DuckDB in production: when it replaces a warehouse
item.description: When an embedded columnar database beats a cloud warehouse for analytics, how to size it, and the failure modes that decide the boundary.

item.title: Chaos engineering without an SRE team
item.description: How to run controlled fault injection in CI without a dedicated SRE team: scoping, kill switches, instrumentation, and failure modes to avoid.

item.title: Multi-agent handoffs: the latency tax nobody measures
item.description: Multi-agent pipelines pay a latency tax at every handoff. Here is how to measure serialisation, transport and re-prompting cost, and what to fix first.

item.title: Route, fine-tune, or scale: pick right
item.description: A practical framework for choosing between model routing, fine-tuning, and simply paying for a larger model, with code, cost math, and evaluation harnesses.

item.title: Agent versioning: the contract you forgot
item.description: Agents expose tool schemas and output shapes as a public interface. Learn how to version that interface, migrate state, and avoid silent caller breakage.

item.title: Settlement vs clearing: backend engineer's guide
item.description: Clearing produces obligations; settlement moves money. How to model both ledgers, reconcile them, and avoid the schema mistakes that break finance.

item.title: Prompt injection: what breaks first in prod
item.description: Why prompt injection defeats prompt-level defenses, and how to bound the blast radius with tool allowlists, argument scoping, URL filtering and confirmation gates.

item.title: Agent architecture: the new model trap
item.description: Newer models made prompt chaining obsolete but not policy enforcement. How to keep a deterministic layer around a capable planner.

item.title: Tech debt: when half your stack is unfamiliar
item.description: A repeatable process for debugging, verifying and governing tools you didn't write, with baselines, contracts, environment measurement and tool cards.
